newsitem.title: GERMANY: Victoria cautiously upbeat for 97 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Victoria cautiously upbeat for 97 earnings.

text.p: German insurer Victoria Holding said on Friday it was cautiously optimistic that its overall earnings would again improve in 1997 after rising by almost 35 percent in 1996.
The company also said it may increase its dividend for 1997 after a payout of 28 percent for 1996.
"We may again be able to pay an increased dividend in 1998 for the 1997 business year," chief executive Edgar Jannott told the insurer's annual general meeting.
Victoria earned a net profit of 116 million marks in 1996.

The company announced on Thursday night it plans to merge with Hamburg-Mannheimer Versicherungs AG, an 80 percent owned subsidiary of Munich Re, in a move that amounts to a Munich Re takeover of Victoria.
The merger will create Germany's second largest primary insurer after Allianz AG.
